title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. U is a smooth geometrically connected curve over a field K finitely generated over Q, of type (g,ν). Its compactification is X = Û, with cusps i in Û∖U. The arithmetic fundamental group sits in the extension (1) 1 → π = π_1(U_{K̄}) → E → Γ = Gal(K̄/K) → 1.

The previous page sets up, for a K-rational cusp i:
- the inertia subgroup L_i ≅ Ẑ(1) = T;
- its centralizer Z(L_i), the cusp decomposition group, fitting into (2) 1 → L_i → Z(L_i) → Γ → 1.

Splittings of (2) exist; for example a uniformizer at i gives one. Their conjugacy classes form a torsor under H^1(Γ, Ẑ(1)) ≅ K^*^ (Kummer theory). Each such splitting gives a 'cuspidal' section of (1). The Proposition states two things. First, if π ≠ 1, cuspidal sections are not π-conjugate to the sections coming from points of U(K). Second, in the anabelian case, cuspidal sections attached to distinct cusps i1 ≠ i2 are distinct.

This page (p. 27 of the notes) sketches the proof.

First claim: fill in the hole i. Pushing forward along π_1(U) → π_1(U'), with U' = U ∪ {i}, turns the cuspidal section into the section of U' attached to the rational point i. It is therefore distinct from the sections of U' attached to the other points of U', in particular the points of U. This uses the injectivity of U'(K) → {sections of U'}, which holds by Kummer theory and Mordell–Weil–Lang–Néron applied to the generalized Jacobian.

Second claim: one wants the same for two cusps, by filling holes. For type (0,3), filling two holes leaves type (0,1), the affine line A^1. Its fundamental group is trivial, so no injectivity statement is available. Equivalently, filling one hole gives G_m, where the first claim breaks down.

Workaround: assume the centralizer statement (3). Let Γ act on π through a splitting of (2), and let Γ^0 be an open subgroup of Γ (presumably). Then π^{Γ^0} = L_i, hence π^Γ = 1, since the cyclotomic character has infinite order. Grothendieck finds this 'hautement plausible' and flags it in the margin as one of the 'questions-clefs'.

Consequence (completed on the next page): the conjugacy class of the section recovers the conjugacy class of L_i, hence the cusp i. A section's centralizer is π^{Γ^0} = 1 for point sections and L_i for cuspidal sections. This gives the dichotomy in the marginal note on p. 28, and leads to Conjecture A (the section conjecture including cuspidal sections).
errors: The first claim, with the stated hypothesis (g,ν) ≠ (0,0),(0,1), is false for type (0,2), U = G_m. There π = Ẑ(1) is abelian, so Z(L_i) = E. Every section of (1) is then a splitting of (2), so the cuspidal sections at 0 (or ∞) include all point sections. The 'boucher le trou' argument also needs injectivity for U', which fails when U' = A^1, i.e. when U is of type (0,2). The correct hypothesis is that U is not of type (0,0), (0,1) or (0,2), e.g. U hyperbolic. This page itself notices the analogous obstruction one step later, for (0,3).
In the first claim the 'a fortiori' clause, comparing with sections that come via subgroups generated by L_i, is unclear. As written it is not a complete argument.

The proof of the second claim for type (0,3) is conditional on (3), which is not proved here. The mild case is handled by reduction to the first claim; distinctness for (0,3) needs a genuinely different input, e.g. weights or the separatedness of cusps in Nakamura or Tamagawa.

ideas.what: Cuspidal sections: splittings of the cusp decomposition group extension (2), forming a torsor under K^*^, and their distinctness from point sections via 'filling the hole' (functoriality along U ⊂ U')
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal sections / packets of cuspidal sections in the section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings, 1983); systematic treatment in J. Stix, Rational Points and Arithmetic of Fundamental Groups (LNM 2054, 2013); also Nakamura, Hoshi
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), mentioning sections at points at infinity; the details here are unpublished

ideas.what: Distinct cusps give non-conjugate inertia/decomposition groups and distinct cuspidal section classes in the anabelian case, with type (0,3) needing special care
ideas.modern_name: separatedness of cusps / injectivity of cusps → conjugacy classes of inertia subgroups

ideas.what: Conjecture (3): the centralizer in π of (an open subgroup of) the image of a cuspidal section is exactly L_i, and π^Γ = 1; for point sections the centralizer is trivial
ideas.modern_name: centralizers of decomposition groups in geometric π_1; commensurable terminality of decomposition groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Nakamura (weight arguments, early 1990s); Mochizuki; Hoshi–Mochizuki

missed.claim: Grothendieck in 1981 explicitly isolates, as a 'question-clef', the centralizer statement π^{Γ^0} = L_i for cuspidal sections, and π^{Γ^0} = 1 for point sections, as the input separating sections. This anticipates Nakamura's later weight-theoretic centralizer results.
missed.quote: à condition d'admettre que pour un scindage de (2), faisant opérer Γ sur π, on a (3) π^{Γ^0} = L_i (donc π^Γ = (1), d'ailleurs) - résultat qui me paraît hautement plausible
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: these statements are now theorems (Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki), so nothing mathematically new remains.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine early working-out of cuspidal sections and their separation, all now standard (Stix's book, Nakamura, Tamagawa). The only notable points are the explicit centralizer conjecture as a 'question-clef', since proved, and a small hypothesis slip for type (0,2).
transcription_corrections: 'dans la section envisagée devient' should read 'la section envisagée devient'.
'pour un sous-groupe de L_i, faisant opérer Γ sur π' should read 'pour un scindage de (2), faisant opérer Γ sur π'. The image shows 'scindage de (2)', and the transcriber misread '(2)' as 'L_i'.
'les classes de conj. de sous-groupes associés à un L_{i1} et un L_{i2}' is more likely 'les classes de conj. de sections (scindages) associées à un L_{i1} et un L_{i2}'.
'par les π-groupes [?] i.e. engendrés par L_i' is uncertain; the sense is 'which come from the subgroups generated by L_i'.
'On voit de même que on [?] constate [?]' should probably read 'On voit de même, ou on constate, que'.
